query_text: what is a good title for a poem I'm writing about a religious boy who has been sheltered from the outside world by his family, but one day he leaves his house and sees the reality of the world?

content.text:
Here are some strong title ideas:

- **“Beyond the Garden Wall”**
- **“The First Sin of Seeing”**
- **“Outside the Prayer Room”**
- **“The World After Amen”**
- **“When the Door Opened”**
- **“Boy of the Locked House”**
- **“The Day Faith Met the Street”**
- **“Unanswered Light”**
- **“Saint at the Window”**
- **“The Gospel of the Outside”**
- **“After the Hymns”**
- **“The World Beneath the Steeple”**
- **“Leaving Eden”**
- **“The House of Halos”**
- **“Eyes Uncovered”**

My favorite for your concept is **“The First Sin of Seeing”** because it captures the boy’s innocence, his religious upbringing, and the idea that simply witnessing the real world feels forbidden.
